sensitivity.note: Train issue <= refit minus 25 months; target end at least 12 months before refit. Latest-vintage inputs still revised.

slope.caveat: Investment-basis Treasury yield minus discount-basis bill rate; own proxy, not NY Fed replication.

credit.formula: Mean of all weekly NFCICREDIT observations whose observation dates fall in the complete calendar month
credit.caveat: Public Chicago Fed conditions index; not a traded credit spread; history revised.

labor.formula: Three-calendar-month UNRATE mean (at least 2observations) minus minimum of 12consecutive such smoothed values, including current
labor.caveat: No interpolation. Explicit available-observation policy handles the missing October 2025 release.

limitations: Latest-vintage historical simulation, not a real-time vintage backtest. UNRATE and NFCI history can be revised.
NBER dates are announced after the fact; recent zero labels can later change. The 25-month eligibility sensitivity delays labels but does not reconstruct historical vintages.
Monthly targets overlap for 12 months; monthly tests are not independent trials. Only four recession episodes occur in the evaluation period.
GS10 minus TB3MS is an investment-basis/discount-basis proxy, not a bond-equivalent or New York Fed replication.
Credit subindex is not a traded credit spread; positive means tighter than average. Its full-history normalization is revised.

Three-calendar-month unemployment averages require at least 2available observations. October 2025 is missing in official data; no value is interpolated. Twelve consecutive smoothed values are required for the labor-gap minimum.
The target includes both new recessions and continuation of an existing recession, not recession onset alone.
Probabilities are model estimates, not certainty or investment advice; stress scenarios are conditional sensitivities, not causal forecasts.

spec.name: Credit-conditioned yield curve
spec.hypothesis: Does the relation between curve inversion and future recession risk depend on contemporaneous credit conditions?
spec.refitFrequency: Annual expanding January refits; current estimate monthly refit
spec.designStatus: One fixed interaction specification proposed after viewing 2023 false alarms. No variant search. Chronological replay is not untouched holdout validation.
caveats: Post-hoc hypothesis: comparisons reuse the sample that motivated the design; prospective evaluation is needed.
Same revised-history and NBER announcement-lag limitations as the original model.
Confirmation is a supplementary decision policy, not a probability model or causal claim.
Cases and regime frequencies are descriptive, not independent validation sets.
The 50/50 original-model/base-rate blend is also post-hoc exploration motivated by historical calibration failure, not independently validated.
Surface support counts overlapping training months and ignores proximity in labor.

surface.supportDefinition: Count of training months within radius 0.35 in training-standardized slope/credit space; labor proximity is not required. Counts are overlapping months, not independent episodes.

spec.name: Rate-path five-input trial
spec.recipe: 0.5 * raw five-input probability + 0.5 * expanding training prevalence
spec.recentPriorRecipe: 0.5 * original three-input probability + 0.5 * recent 180-calendar-month training prevalence
spec.recentPriorDefinition: Mean known binary targets on complete original-three-input issues in 180 consecutive calendar months ending at formal issue/refit minus 13 months; requires full 15-year calendar span and at least 120 observed eligible months. Window boundaries do not slide when recent labels are missing.
spec.recentPriorDesignStatus: Second distinct hypothesis specified before its scoring after the first rate-path candidate was evaluated; no tuning after seeing this second result. It remains exploratory, not untouched holdout evidence.
spec.annualRefit: January; expanding window; target ends strictly before refit
spec.designStatus: One specification, fixed weights and comparison windows set before calculating these trial results. The wider project was motivated by historical failures, so this remains exploratory latest-vintage replay, not untouched or real-time validation.
spec.comparatorPolicy: Official original annual forecasts, their expanding base and fixed 50/50 blend, on the exact common issue dates. Candidate uses its own complete-five training prevalence; matched-three ablations share that training sample and prevalence.
spec.improvementSign: Positive differences mean lower candidate/raw-five error than the named comparator.
limitations: The target includes continuation of an existing recession, not onset alone.
Revised observations and retrospectively dated NBER labels remain; target purging does not reconstruct historical vintages or announcement availability.
Monthly outcomes overlap and recent slices contain few independent downturns.
The fixed blend is an experimental probability recipe, not independently validated calibration.
No missing observations are interpolated; endpoint changes require the exact calendar-month endpoints.

recentPriorGate.criterion: Recent blend must beat official fixed-three blend and expanding base in both all and 2016-onward windows; incremental model contribution additionally requires beating its own recent-prior-only control in both.
recentPriorGate.note: Changing the prior can help without incremental value from the raw model. Compare both controls; no main-model promotion or future-performance claim follows from this historical experiment.

publicationGate.criterion: Candidate Brier must beat both official fixed-three blend and official expanding base in BOTH all-history and precommitted 2016-onward windows.
publicationGate.note: A passed retrospective screen is not prospective validation. No post-result feature, weight or window search is permitted.

spec.recipe: 0.5 * official original probability + 0.5 * smoothed recent credit-labor regime prior
spec.canonicalization: Round credit and labor inputs to 10 decimal places before credit>0 and labor>=0.50 classification; original model probabilities are unchanged.
spec.controls: Same-date official fixed blend; recent unconditioned blend; expanding four-state prior/blend with 24 pseudo issue-months; dynamic prior alone.
spec.designStatus: Fixed state thresholds, window, strength and mixture specified before this experiment was scored. It remains exploratory latest-vintage chronological replay.
spec.adaptiveRecipe: recentBlend + alpha * (fixedRegimeBlend - recentBlend); original probability retains 50% weight
spec.adaptiveFit: alpha=clip(sum((c-a)*(y-a))/sum((c-a)^2),0,1), from previously issued annual forecasts whose full 12-month targets end strictly before refit; minimum 60, otherwise zero; zero denominator also zero.
spec.adaptiveDesignStatus: This second approach was specified before its scoring, after observing the first fixed-rule result. No further variants or threshold search are permitted; it is not untouched holdout evidence.
spec.target: At least one recession month in the following 12 months, including continuation; not onset-only.
spec.improvementSign: brierDeltaVsIncumbent=candidate minus incumbent (negative better); brierImprovement=incumbent minus candidate (positive better); relative is that improvement divided by incumbent Brier.
limitations: Original inputs are already lagged two months at issue; no additional lag or contemporaneous new data is used.
Current and historical priors use retrospective revised labels; calendar purging does not reconstruct announcement delays.
Four-state counts and pseudo issue-months are overlapping observations, not independent business cycles.
Sparse/empty states shrink toward the same-window pool; an empty cell equals the pool exactly.

notes: Onset is the first monthly USREC value of one following a zero. With this convention the 2020 onset is March, after the February NBER peak.
A row is classified only if the official outcome and all thirteen monthly USREC labels from the issue month through the horizon end are present.
Lead distances and phase assignments use hindsight only for evaluation. Each forecast uses its dated inputs.
Calibration includes all scored expansion-issued months with classified outcomes. Each model uses its own probability bins, with 100% included in the final bin.
Conditioning on a future recession selects positive windows. The observed event rate in such windows is one by construction.
Adjacent twelve-month horizons overlap. Episode paths count only observed issues, and a single recession can contribute multiple positives.

spec.fitClock: Past annual out-of-fold predictions only. The full twelve-month outcome window ends strictly before each refit. Historical weights refit each January and live weights refit monthly.

notes: The site’s fixed 30% threshold applies to every forecast. An alert includes equality.
First alert lead is measured from the earliest flagged expansion issue in the twelve months before onset. A previously elevated alert can qualify.
A new crossing requires an observed below-threshold forecast one calendar month earlier. A previous forecast outside the score window is used only to identify crossings.
Mean lead uses all complete twelve-month episodes. A missed episode contributes zero. Partial or unavailable episodes remain visible and are excluded from this mean.
Quiet false-alarm rate is the fraction of paired expansion issues with no recession in the next twelve months that nevertheless raised an alert.
The timing test requires a longer mean lead, at least as many detected complete episodes and no higher quiet false-alarm rate, in both evaluation windows.

spec.probability: Use the expansion-onset model probability with its original half-weight historical prior.
spec.issuedPath: Reprice four consecutive issue-month feature vectors using the current issue’s fit and prior. Each feature date is two months before its source issue.
spec.rule: The 30% alarm always fires. Below 30%, require at least 20%, a rising latest month, a positive three-month change, and a continuation of the three-month average pace to 30% within the specified projection horizon.
spec.missing: If any path score is missing, use the level rule alone. A missing current probability leaves all decisions unavailable.
spec.precision: Compare risks at twelve decimal places. Level and projected threshold comparisons include equality.
spec.evaluation: Score all policies on the same mature expansion origins. Require earlier warning in a complete episode, no later complete warnings and zero additional quiet alert-months in both windows. Report strictly earlier mean lead in both separately.

prospective.note: Each receipt freezes the first available monthly fit, four dated input vectors, one conditional probability and three warning decisions. Only closed thirteen-month USREC windows with an expansion origin enter the scores. Revised dates can change outcomes.

spec.scope: Keep each level alarm and each published conditional probability. Test confirmation only on extra three-month pace alarms.
spec.pressure: Require negative six-month permit growth, positive twelve-month initial-claims growth, and a credit index higher than three months earlier.
spec.direction: Require permit growth below its value three months earlier, claims growth above its value three months earlier, and a higher credit index.
spec.breadth: Require at least two of the three pressure votes. All three votes must be observed.
spec.precision: Round each input to twelve decimal places before strict sign and direction comparisons. Equality gives no confirmation.
spec.clock: Each input belongs to the observation month two calendar months before its forecast issue. Use the exact third prior month for changes.
spec.missing: Missing required votes disable the extra alert for that rule. A missing probability leaves all decisions unavailable.
spec.test: Keep the May 2000 alert and at least eleven months of lead before April 2001, exceed the level rule’s lead, preserve complete detections, and add zero quiet alerts in both windows.

recipe.scope: Keep each level alarm and each published conditional probability. Test confirmation only on extra three-month pace alarms.
recipe.pressure: Require negative six-month permit growth, positive twelve-month initial-claims growth, and a credit index higher than three months earlier.
recipe.direction: Require permit growth below its value three months earlier, claims growth above its value three months earlier, and a higher credit index.
recipe.breadth: Require at least two of the three pressure votes. All three votes must be observed.
recipe.precision: Round each input to twelve decimal places before strict sign and direction comparisons. Equality gives no confirmation.
recipe.clock: Each input belongs to the observation month two calendar months before its forecast issue. Use the exact third prior month for changes.
recipe.missing: Missing required votes disable the extra alert for that rule. A missing probability leaves all decisions unavailable.
recipe.test: Keep the May 2000 alert and at least eleven months of lead before April 2001, exceed the level rule’s lead, preserve complete detections, and add zero quiet alerts in both windows.

paceRecipe.probability: Use the expansion-onset model probability with its original half-weight historical prior.
paceRecipe.issuedPath: Reprice four consecutive issue-month feature vectors using the current issue’s fit and prior. Each feature date is two months before its source issue.
paceRecipe.rule: The 30% alarm always fires. Below 30%, require at least 20%, a rising latest month, a positive three-month change, and a continuation of the three-month average pace to 30% within the specified projection horizon.
paceRecipe.missing: If any path score is missing, use the level rule alone. A missing current probability leaves all decisions unavailable.
paceRecipe.precision: Compare risks at twelve decimal places. Level and projected threshold comparisons include equality.
paceRecipe.evaluation: Score all policies on the same mature expansion origins. Require earlier warning in a complete episode, no later complete warnings and zero additional quiet alert-months in both windows. Report strictly earlier mean lead in both separately.

prospective.note: Each record freezes one conditional probability, the common four-month path, the permit, claims and credit votes and all five decisions. The level and pace controls use the same capture vintage as the confirmation rules. Scoring uses 13 closed USREC months and includes expansion origins. Revised labels can change scoring.

prospective.note: First captures are frozen at their actual UTC capture time. Outcomes stay pending until all 12 future USREC months are published. Hash-linked public Git receipts provide an inspectable audit trail, not tamper-proof storage or an independent timestamp.

spec.decomposition: Flatness change equals the rise in the three-month bill yield minus the rise in the ten-year yield. Positive values mean flattening. Preserve negative offsetting legs.
spec.shortLead: Net flattening with a positive bill rise that strictly exceeds the negative of the ten-year yield change.
spec.bear: Short-led flattening with the ten-year yield flat or rising.
spec.sustained: Short-led flattening with a strictly rising bill yield in each of the three consecutive monthly steps.
spec.mixedTwoToOne: Post-hoc shadow rule. Require positive flattening, a rising bill, a flat or falling ten-year yield, and a bill rise at least twice the size of the long-yield fall. Equality qualifies.
spec.design: The first three rules were fixed before this replay. The fourth was specified after reviewing the known cases and extra quiet months. Its historical fit can be evaluated but prospective validation starts at first capture.
spec.scope: Apply these rules only to the extra three-month pace warning below 30%. Keep every level warning and use the same conditional probability.
spec.clock: Use four exact monthly average observations. The last observation precedes the issue month by two months.
spec.precision: Round observed yields to twelve decimal places and compare changes in integer units. A tie does not qualify as short-led.
spec.missing: The first two filters require both yield endpoints. The sustained filter also requires the two intervening bill observations. Missing required data block only supplemental alerts.
spec.test: Require the May 2000 warning, at least eleven months of lead and an advance over the level alarm for 2001, preserved complete detections and no additional quiet alerts in either sample.
